headlines.snippet: It has been cleared for publication that Sergeant Ron Jonathan Reitman and Sergeant Yuval Shay Suilem fell in a terrorist attack at the Etzion junction. Reitman, 23, from Ashkelon, and Suilem, 20, from Hod Hasharon, served in the Ari Battalion of the Hatifet Brigade. Three other soldiers were moderately and lightly wounded. The IDF estimates that the terrorists planned a major attack against civilians, which was prevented by the soldiers' actions. The two terrorists were neutralized, and a foreign photographer is suspected of prior knowledge of the attack. Netanyahu ordered an immediate lockdown of Hebron and preparations for a full closure of the West Bank.

headlines.snippet: The citizens of Iran are preparing for the resumption of war by hoarding food and avoiding unnecessary travel. Due to growing fears of further escalation, Tehran residents told The New York Times about their terror and preparations. Citizens are flocking to gas stations, withdrawing cash, and reporting sick to avoid work. One Iranian man said, 'I told my wife not to wake our son in the morning and to leave him at home.' A teacher from Tehran added, 'I think about how I can protect my students, so they won't be afraid if there are explosions during lessons.'

headlines.snippet: After a very close battle, President Lula won the elections in Brazil. Drama in South America: the incumbent president defeated the right-wing candidate Bolsonaro in the second round and will continue in office. Bolsonaro led after the first round, but Lula managed to surprise. 'We managed to convince that the vote is of paramount importance, and we prevented foreign interference,' Lula said in his victory speech. Bolsonaro refused to concede defeat. The election results will determine the relationship with Israel in the continent's largest country.
